identity.memory_hook: Mega Glalie threatens to detonate beside a trapping Toxapex, then Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle turn the apparent stall battle into a no-setter speed assault.
identity.story_fit: Glacia treats cold as pressure that seals exits and punishes stillness. Four cold-climate attackers, a venomous deep-water anchor, and a Flash Fire specter express that idea without repeating the familiar snow-and-Aurora-Veil script.
identity.primary_player_question: Can the player scout or deny Mega Glalie's detonation while preventing Toxapex from trapping and poisoning the answer that must survive for Glacia's fast back line?
identity.primary_mode: Mega Glalie and Toxapex open together. Refrigerate Double-Edge or Explosion creates immediate physical pressure while Baneful Bunker, Infestation, Toxic, and Wide Guard turn passive or overprotective play into a clock.
identity.secondary_mode: Chien-Pao, Choice Scarf Chandelure, Focus Sash Mamoswine, and Booster Energy Iron Bundle form a mixed no-dedicated-speed-control offense whose priority, pivots, item states, and Sword of Ruin pressure reward positioning rather than one field button.
identity.preview_pressure: The player must respect both a two-target Mega detonation and a long trap clock at the opening, yet cannot spend every speed and priority resource before Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle appear.

difficulty.rationale: Six optimized level-82 to level-85 Pokemon combine a credible double-KO threat, a trap and Toxic clock, a major Ice legendary, two priority users, a Choice Scarf Fire immunity, and a Booster Energy speed apex. Broad counterplay exists, but a blind loss is expected because preserving the wrong answer for the wrong mode is costly.

difficulty.resource_tax: Glacia enters as the third League member without automatic healing. Infestation, Toxic, repeated switching, detonation scouting, priority, and mixed coverage tax HP, status cures, speed-control PP, Sash-breaking tools, and whatever carried recovery the player chooses to spend before Drake.

Only then reconsider a coverage move or strategic mode

ordering.mandatory_order_reason: Glalie and Toxapex must be the visible opening so detonation and trapping define the fight immediately. The reserves intentionally alternate physical, special, physical, and special pressure; they do not require a fabricated guaranteed pair, but smart switching must not casually dismantle the opening before it presents a real decision.

custom_requirements: Reward Refrigerate Explosion only when Toxapex or the current ally has selected protection, is immune, or the expected two-target payoff justifies losing Glalie; otherwise prefer Double-Edge, Ice Shard, Protect, or preservation.

Select Infestation and Toxic against a target that can actually be trapped and poisoned, avoid redundant clocks, recognize Baneful Bunker as the safe Explosion partner action, and use Wide Guard only against credible spread pressure.
Permit Toxapex to switch for Regenerator when the clock is established or its board role is exhausted, without abandoning an active trap at random.
Exploit Chandelure's Choice Scarf and Trick, and recognize that Sword of Ruin exposes Chien-Pao's partner as well as opposing Pokemon.
Treat Booster Energy and Quark Drive as automatic state, and use Flip Turn when preserving Iron Bundle creates more value than direct damage.
forbidden_behaviors: Do not choose Explosion into an unprotected vulnerable ally merely because it has high base power.
Do not force Explosion when Double-Edge, Ice Shard, switching, or protecting preserves a winning Glalie.
Do not use Infestation on an already trapped target or Toxic on an immune or already poisoned target.
Do not spam Wide Guard without a credible opposing spread move.
Do not switch Toxapex while doing so silently releases the only valuable active trap.
Do not repeatedly attack into a Choice-locked immunity with Chandelure.
ai.state_machine: Mode A fixes Mega Glalie beside Toxapex. Glalie evaluates direct pressure, protection, or a safe detonation while Toxapex establishes at most one meaningful trap and poison clock or shields the board. Mode B begins when the lead breaks: Chien-Pao and Chandelure apply raw fast physical and special pressure without a speed setter, while Mamoswine and Iron Bundle preserve priority, Sash, Booster Energy, and pivot resources for the final exchanges.

counterplay.intentional_weakness: The team has no snow setter, Aurora Veil, Tailwind, Trick Room, or redirection; Taunt and status prevention can blank Toxapex, common Fighting, Steel, Rock, Water, Grass, and priority attacks pressure Mega Glalie, Sword of Ruin exposes Chien-Pao's partner, and Chandelure's Choice lock plus Mamoswine's Sash create visible item seams.
counterplay.first_loss_lesson: Do not treat Toxapex as harmless support or assume Glalie must explode immediately. Scout the detonation, deny the trap or Toxic clock, and preserve a speed-control or priority answer for Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle.
classes: Protect, Ghost immunity, resist switching, Fake Out, or focused priority to scout or stop Mega Glalie's detonation turn
Taunt, Encore, Substitute, Misty Terrain, Safeguard, poison immunity, trapping denial, or fast focus fire against Toxapex
Icy Wind, Electroweb, paralysis, Trick Room, priority, Choice Scarf users, or raw faster threats against the no-setter fast mode
Fighting, Steel, Fire, Rock, and Water pressure distributed across the Ice attackers, with Ground or Dark pressure checking Toxapex and Chandelure differently
Knock Off, Trick, hazards, multihit moves, and Choice-lock exploitation against the item-dependent seams

Chandelure is Choice-locked, Mamoswine depends on an intact Sash, and Iron Bundle consumes Booster Energy automatically
unacceptable_failure_modes: No hidden required catch, immunity, or exact first-turn sequence may be necessary.
The AI may not read an unrevealed player action to decide whether Explosion is safe.
Accuracy misses from Icicle Crash or Hydro Pump may not be the primary source of difficulty.
Toxic and Infestation may not become an unavoidable infinite stall loop.
The fight may not gain a second Mega or any non-Mega gimmick.
If the AI cannot execute detonation and trapping honestly, the design must be revised rather than scripted to cheat.

identity.memory_hook: Stealth Rock and two Choice-locked Dragons tax every preservation decision before a special Mega Dragonite reverses the expected wall and Zygarde asks whether the player saved one true endgame answer.
identity.story_fit: Drake's existing dialogue already frames Pokemon partnership as a singles duel where every choice must stand on its own. Six Dragons with distinct sequential jobs turn that speech into a concrete preservation test rather than a legendary-stat exhibition.
identity.primary_player_question: Can the player preserve the correct Ice, Fairy, status, or Unaware answer through Stealth Rock, two Choice-locked lures, and mixed damage long enough to stop both Mega Dragonite and the final Power Construct Zygarde?
identity.primary_mode: Rough Skin Rocky Helmet Garchomp establishes Stealth Rock and phazes greed; Choice Band Dragapult and Choice Scarf Hydreigon then force fast physical and special trades while pivoting out of bad locks.
identity.secondary_mode: Assault Vest Adaptability Dragalge punishes the Fairy answer, special Mega Dragonite breaks the physical wall the opening invites, and Leftovers Power Construct Zygarde is the one deliberate setup-and-paralysis endgame.
identity.preview_pressure: The all-Dragon roster invites Ice and Fairy offense, but the player must decide which answer can survive Garchomp's Fire lure, Hydreigon's Flash Cannon, Dragalge's Poison pressure, special Mega Dragonite, and Zygarde's separate physical endgame.

difficulty.rationale: Six optimized level-82 to level-86 Pokemon cover physical, special, fast, bulky, pivoting, lure, Mega, and legendary endgame roles without adding a second gimmick. Difficulty comes from irreversible preservation mistakes: Stealth Rock taxes correction, the two Choice users punish the wrong immunity, Dragalge removes the easy Fairy shortcut, Mega Dragonite reverses the expected defensive category, and Zygarde demands one surviving endgame plan.

ordering.mandatory_order_reason: Garchomp must present the hazard and phazing tax before the two Choice commitments. Dragalge is deliberately positioned before special Mega Dragonite so the player is invited to preserve a physical wall, and Zygarde remains the final independent setup question. Smart switching may answer a bad matchup, but it may not casually spend the climax out of sequence.

custom_requirements: Prefer Stealth Rock on global turn zero only when Garchomp survives and the hazard has value; prefer Dragon Tail against a credible setup state or a switch worth taxing, not as blind low-accuracy damage.
Track Dragapult's Band and Hydreigon's Scarf locks, use U-turn to escape losing locks, and switch rather than repeatedly choose an immune or heavily resisted target.
Activate Mega Dragonite as the one Mega, value Roost when it can restore a meaningful Multiscale threshold, and recognize its special rather than physical damage role.
Use Glare when paralysis changes the endgame, Coil only when Zygarde survives the reply and gains real sweeping value, and Outrage only when its lock is an acceptable commitment.
Preserve the sequential lure structure: do not reveal or sacrifice Zygarde merely because its raw BST is high while earlier role-specific answers remain healthy.
forbidden_behaviors: Do not force Stealth Rock when Garchomp will faint before acting or immediate damage wins the position.
Do not repeatedly select a Choice-locked move into an immunity or extreme resistance.
Do not Mega Evolve a second Pokemon or treat Dragonite as a physical Dragon Dance set it does not carry.
Do not use Roost at full HP or when Mega Dragonite cannot survive the turn.
Do not use Coil when Haze, phazing, Encore, an immediate Ice KO, or another visible denial makes setup worthless.
Do not use Glare into status immunity, Coil into immediate denial or an Ice knockout, or Outrage while its lock gives the player a free Fairy answer.
ai.state_machine: Phase A opens with Garchomp's conditional hazard and phazing tax. Phase B cycles the two readable Choice commitments: Dragapult supplies physical speed and Hydreigon supplies special speed plus a Fairy lure, with U-turn or smart switching escaping bad locks. Phase C uses Dragalge to punish the obvious Fairy response, then special Mega Dragonite reverses the expected defensive category. Phase D uses Glare to change an otherwise losing speed exchange and permits Zygarde to Coil or commit to Outrage only when the endgame is genuinely safe.

counterplay.intentional_weakness: Every member is a Dragon, so Ice and Fairy offense remain structurally excellent once the legal lures are identified; Dragapult and Hydreigon expose Choice locks, the roster has no cleric, hazard removal, screen, weather, terrain, or second setup sweeper, Multiscale can be broken by chip, and Zygarde deliberately uses Earthquake rather than unsupported Thousand Arrows so Flying, Levitate, and Air Balloon remain real answers.
counterplay.first_loss_lesson: Record which attackers are Choice-locked, scout the anti-Fairy Flash Cannon and Sludge Bomb lures, and stop spending the dedicated Zygarde answer merely to win an earlier trade. Break Multiscale before trying to burst Mega Dragonite.
classes: hazard denial or removal, Magic Bounce, Taunt, and heavy immediate pressure against lead Garchomp
Fairy and Ice offense combined with careful scouting of Hydreigon's Flash Cannon, Dragalge's Poison STAB, and Fire coverage

burn, Intimidate, Reflect, physical walls, and Rocky Helmet against Dragapult, Garchomp, and Zygarde; special walls against Hydreigon, Dragalge, and Mega Dragonite
Haze, Clear Smog, Unaware, phazing, Encore, Taunt, Trick, status immunity, and strong Ice pressure against the final Glare and Coil Zygarde
chip damage, hazards, status, priority, or a sacrificial weak hit to break Mega Dragonite's Multiscale before the decisive attack
